evidence: Timeline (notify-log.txt): wall #1 06:29:21 after 75 of 526 terms, 2912 raw rows (= queue c98b2a); Brad cleared it; pull resumed; wall #2 06:41:51 after 107 terms total, 4259 raw rows (= this item); wall #3 09:00:56 after 6 searches of a full 526-term re-pull, 0 rows (desktop notify only, no queue item; pull-order-walmart.txt rebuilt 08:55:39 for that attempt).

The partial WAS admitted, by design: out\regular\walmart-regular-2026-08-06.json holds 2556 priced rows from 107 terms (4259 raw -> 2556 after rejects; walmart-rejects-2026-08-06.json), stamped pull_terms=107, captured=2026-08-06. NOTHING was quarantined (out\throttled holds only family-fare-2026-08-06 today). The alert's 'go stale (or get quarantined)' is template text; the actual outcome was union carry.

The 14-day union is real and held the board: 419 Walmart cells on comparison-2026-08-06 vs 414 on comparison-2026-08-05, ZERO cells lost, 5 gained. Union file set (deals): 07-23 (1328), 07-25 (1351), 07-29 (2784), 07-30 (4244), 07-31 (4863), 08-01 (4881), 08-05 (1209), 08-06 (2556). Cell backing by newest union file containing the exact item+price: 141 cells 08-06, 5 cells 08-05, 266 cells 08-01, 1 cell 07-31, 6 cells 07-25.

No thin-capture eviction: audit-capture-eviction.ps1 run live at ~11:52 against the 11:23:15 board reports '2842 published cell(s), 7370 dated candidate row(s), 0 cell(s) dearer than the engine's own eligibility rule allows at or above 1.25x'. Positive control: its -SelfTest passes ('SELF-TEST PASS (2 must-fire, 5 clean twins)' - the frozen Sams baby-formula eviction still fires, the onions stale-low twin stays silent). The 10:22:08 run against the 10:21:49 generation was also 0 findings and is committed (88b4093).

Dates are honest at the engine layer: Walmart rows in candidates-2026-08-06.json carry src_date equal to their capture file's date (2045 x 08-06, 154 x 08-05, 2880 x 08-01, 102 x 07-31, 2 x 07-30, 390 x 07-25 - no row re-stamped to look fresher), and the 11:32:17 guards run passes 'no published price claims a date newer than the capture it came from (as_of evidence)'. PRE-EXISTING CAVEAT, documented not new: walmart-regular-2026-08-01.json is a merged carry-forward - 4694 of its 4881 rows are identical item+price to 07-31, and 2028 rows carry internal as_of 07-30/07-31 which compare-deals deliberately ignores for Walmart (compare-deals.ps1:442-453, a measured decision: honoring it moved 3 cells ~2x wrong). So '266 cells backed by 08-01' means observed 07-30/31 in nearly all cases. audit-walmart-fullpull correctly treats 08-01 as partial (pull_terms=21) and ages the watch off 07-31, which is conservative in the right direction.

Board effect of the day, measured: 59 Walmart cells moved vs the 08-05 board (41 cheaper, 18 dearer; extremes turkey-lunchmeat 0.8943 -> 0.2794 cheaper, broccoli 1.3257 -> 2.1208 dearer). Dearer movers are either the same product at a fresh price (eggs: same 'Great Value Large White Eggs, 60 Count' 1.426 -> 1.624/each from the 08-06 pull) or survivors after yesterday's cheaper row lost eligibility or was ruled known-wrong by the morning's depth-rule work; the 0-findings eviction audit is the proof that no surviving cell is dearer than the engine's own rule allows. The arrivals watcher flagged the notable ones for review at 11:28:33 (frozen-broccoli CROWN, chicken-breast) - the review queue is doing its job.

Resume ledger: pull-order-walmart.txt (526 staples-first terms) supports resuming at any index, and resume DID work within the live session (75 -> 107 after Brad cleared wall #1). But notify-ack-walmart.json ('user dismissed the prompt - treat as clearance to resume', written 09:46:40) has NO consumer outside a live pull session (grep the tree: only notify-desktop.ps1 touches notify-ack-* files), and the weekly run was already past capture (lock phase 'links' since 06:56). The 09:46 clearance resumed nothing: no Walmart capture exists after 06:42:30.

Forward risk, from the estate's own watch (ad-cycle-log 11:32:42): newest comprehensive capture walmart-regular-2026-07-31.json (217 terms) is 6 days old; advisory fires at 10 days = 2026-08-10; union cliff at 14. The 08-01 file leaves the union on the 2026-08-16 board, at which point the ~266 cells it backs expire unless the Wednesday 2026-08-12 pull (or an earlier cleared-wall rescue) lands a comprehensive capture. Near-term exposure is small: 6 of 417 attributed cells expire within 5 days, under the 5% warn.

GUARDS: the settled board is green - 'GUARDS OK: every hard invariant holds' at 11:32:17, page published 11:32:40 (deals-page.sig), 'watchers ok: every guard still fires on its own founding bug' at 11:35:41. surface_fix.what: Roster audit-capture-eviction.ps1 into check-ad-cycles.ps1's per-cycle audit sweep, non-blocking, so the ONLY check that can see a partial-pull eviction runs on every board generation instead of only when a human remembers it. Today it ran at 10:22:08 by hand and would never have re-checked the 11:23:15 generation on its own; this review re-ran it by hand again.
surface_fix.exact_change: In the audit sweep where walmart-fullpull is called (the 11:32:42 slot in today's log), add a logged call to audit-capture-eviction.ps1 with log prefix 'capture-eviction:'; surface the findings count in the cycle summary the way fullpull's line is surfaced; advisory only - do NOT gate the publish on it (the engine rule enforces eligibility and guards already fail closed; this is the outcome watch). Mind the 2026-07-30 lesson: capture the child's output without 2>&1-under-EAP=Stop killing the cycle.

items.root_cause: The wall is PerimeterX behavior detection on walmart.com's search endpoint; it re-arms unpredictably (held for 34 terms after the first clearance, then for 6 searches after the 08:55 full re-pull) and clearing it is Brad's, never ours - bypass is a hard stop. The estate's designed absorption (staples-first pull order, admit-partials-with-pull_terms, 14-day union, the coverage-depth rule shipped this morning) handled every consequence today, now MEASURED rather than assumed. Two structural residues make the condition worth code at all: (1) audit-capture-eviction, the outcome guard for exactly the class a partial pull threatens, is not rostered in any scheduled cycle - only its -SelfTest runs via test-auditors - so the eviction check is hand-cranked in an estate where partials are now routine; (2) the resume handshake is session-scoped: notify-ack-walmart.json has no consumer once the pull session moves on, while the alert text promises resume-on-clearance, so Brad's 09:46 clearance click was silently wasted. No data was lost to (2) today; the cost was a missed chance to shrink the 419-term deficit (526 - 107) before 08-12.
items.root_fix_note: surface_fix IS the root fix for residue (1). Residue (2) is deliberately NOT fixed this round: building an ack-polling resume daemon is new machinery for a case whose damage is bounded by the union window, the 08-10 fullpull advisory, and the 08-12 weekly cadence. Revisit only if a wasted clearance actually costs a refresh cycle. Record it, do not build it.

The 107-term/2556-row partial was admitted into the 14-day union by design, nothing quarantined; board held 419 Walmart cells (up from 414), backed 141 by 08-06 / 5 by 08-05 / 266 by the 08-01 carry-forward / 7 older; audit-capture-eviction: 0 findings on the live board with a passing self-test; src_date stamping honest per capture file; GUARDS OK 11:32:17. The wall stays with Brad. Shipped: audit-capture-eviction rostered into the daily cycle so the eviction outcome check runs on every generation. Watch: fullpull advisory arms 2026-08-10 off the 07-31 comprehensive capture; union cliff 2026-08-16 costs ~266 cells if the 08-12 weekly pull walls without a cleared challenge.

items.deviation: THE CODE SHIPPED EXACTLY AS PLANNED. The deviation is in the evidence basis underneath it: the Walmart wall was CLEARED and a rescue pull landed mid-implementation, which is the branch the plan's own freshness line named ('If a NEW Walmart capture lands before implementation, re-run audit-capture-eviction before shipping'). Timeline: my step-1 premise check at 11:50 found the 11:23:15 board and the 06:42:30 capture exactly as pinned, so I edited; by 11:57:16 a resumed pull had rewritten out\regular\walmart-regular-2026-08-06.json from pull_terms=107 / 2556 deals (the version at HEAD 9f36abde) to pull_terms=420 / 11092 deals, and a concurrent session rebuilt the board at built_at 2026-08-06T11:58:57. WHAT I MEASURED ON THE NEW GENERATION, not assumed: (1) nothing was lost to the overwrite, Walmart priced cells went 419 -> 435; (2) I re-ran audit-capture-eviction.ps1 myself rather than trusting the 11:59:00 artifact a concurrent actor left behind, and it reports '2858 published cell(s), 11922 dated candidate row(s), 0 cell(s) dearer than the engine's own eligibility rule allows at or above 1.25x', rc 0, so the 0-findings premise holds on the post-rescue board too and the coverage-depth rule again absorbed a capture swap without an eviction; (3) audit-walmart-fullpull now reads 'newest comprehensive capture walmart-regular-2026-08-06.json (420 terms) is 0 day(s) old', with 1 of 435 attributed Walmart cells expiring within 5 days and 0 untraceable. THAT FALSIFIES THE PLAN'S FORWARD-RISK WATCH, in the good direction: the comprehensive clock reset today, so the 2026-08-10 advisory and the 2026-08-16 union cliff both retire (advisory now 2026-08-16, cliff 2026-08-20), and the ~266 cells riding the 08-01 carry-forward are no longer the exposure the plan described. WHAT I DID: shipped both hunks unchanged, since rostering a read-only audit is orthogonal to board state and the premise held on BOTH generations; amended the queue resolution_note so the stale watch line does not outlive the condition; and left open_questions_for_brad answered by events rather than re-asking him to clear a wall he has already cleared. NOT A NEW CLASS and deliberately not bounced: this is the same PerimeterX wall the plan understands, resolving in the direction the plan hoped for, with no new mechanism for the board to be wrong. I did NOT rebuild or republish the board (ship_sequence step 6 stands): I made no board-affecting change, the rebuild at 11:58:57 belongs to the concurrent rescue session with Chrome and PowerShell processes still live at 12:01, and publishing another session's in-flight work is exactly the fight the concurrency rule says not to pick.
